questions.q: The chemical composition of 'slag' formed during the smelting process in the extraction of copper is
questions.solution: During the extraction of copper, iron is present in the ore as impurity (FeS). The ore together with a little coke and silica is smelted; FeS present as impurity in the ore is oxidized to iron oxide, which then reacts with silica to form fusible ferrous silicate which is removed as slag. $2 \mathrm{FeS}+3 \mathrm{O}_2 \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{FeO}+2 \mathrm{SO}_2 \uparrow$

questions.q: The reaction that does NOT take place in a blast furnace between $900 \mathrm{ K}$ to $1500 \mathrm{ K}$ temperature range during extraction of iron is :
questions.solution:
At $900-1500 \mathrm{ K}$ (higher temperature range in the blast furnace)
Reaction which take place are:
$\mathrm{C}+\mathrm{CO}_2 \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{CO}$
$\mathrm{FeO}+\mathrm{CO} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Fe}+\mathrm{CO}_2$
$\mathrm{CaO}+\mathrm{SiO}_2 \longrightarrow \mathrm{CaSiO}_3$ (Slag formation)
$\mathrm{Fe}_2 \mathrm{O}_3+\mathrm{CO} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{FeO}+\mathrm{CO}_2$ at $500-800 \mathrm{ K}$

questions.q: $\Delta_{f} \mathrmG^{-}$ vs $\mathrm{T}$ plot in the Ellingham diagram slopes downward for the reaction
questions.solution: $\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{s})+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{O}_{2}(\mathrm{ g}) \rightarrow \mathrm{CO}(\mathrm{g}) ; \Delta \mathrm{S}$ increases. Hence, as the temperature increases, $\mathrm{T} \Delta \mathrm{S}$ increases and hence $\Delta \mathrm{G}(\Delta \mathrm{H}-\mathrm{T} \Delta \mathrm{S})$ decreases. In other words, the slope of the curve for formation of CO decreases. However, for all other oxides, it increases.

questions.q: The final step for extraction of copper from copper pyrite in bessemer converter involves the reaction
questions.solution:
In Bessemer converter, copper-sulphide is partially oxidised to cuprous oxide, which further reacts with the remaining copper sulphide to give copper and sulphur di oxide, i.e. ${Cu}_{2}S + 2{Cu}_{2}O ⟶ 6Cu + {SO}_{2}$

This reaction represents auto reduction. ${Cu}_{2}O$ reacts with ${Cu}_{2}S$& to give copper metal. The solid metal obtained is called as blister copper and is about 99% pure.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Metals
questions.q: In the context of the Hall-Heroult process for the extraction of $Al$, Which of the following statements is incorrect.
options: $CO$ and ${CO}_{2}$ are produced in the process.
${Al}_{2}{O}_{3}$ is mixed with ${CaF}_{2}$ which lowers the melting point of the mixture and brings conductivity.
${Al}^{3 +}$ is reduced at the cathode to form $Al$.
questions.solution:
(i) In Hall-Heroult process for extraction of $Al$, carbon anode is oxidised to $CO$ and ${CO}_{2}$.

(ii) When ${Al}_{2}{O}_{3}$ is mixed with ${CaF}_{2}$, it lowers the melting point of the mixture and brings conductivity.

(iii) ${Al}^{3 +}$ is reduced at cathode to form $Al$.

(iv) ${Al}_{2}{O}_{3}$ serves as the electrolyte, undergoing the redox process. ${Na}_{3}{AlF}_{6}$ although is an electrolyte but serves as a solvent, not electrolyte.

questions.q: Which of the following reactions is an example of calcination process?
questions.solution:
The process of conversion of a concentrated ore into its oxide by heating in absence of or in limited supply of air is called calcination. It is usually done for hydroxide, hydrated oxides and carbonate ores.

${MgCO}_{3}\overset{\Delta}{⟶}MgO + {CO}_{2}\left(g\right)$

questions.q: Which of the following metal is leached by cyanide process&
questions.solution:
Cyanide process, which is also known as MacArthur cyanide process involves the extraction of gold and silver from their ores by dissolving them in a dilute solution of sodium cyanide or potassium cyanide.& The leaching is carried out in the presence of air or oxygen to oxidise the metal.

$Ag$ is leached by cyanide process by making the complex using $NaCN / KCN$ as follows

${Ag}_{2}S + 4NaCN ⟶ 2\mathop{Na\left[Ag ( CN{)}_{2}\right]}_{Soluble} + {Na}_{2}S$
